public_rationale: Prominent contemporaneous records explicitly considered slower progress. That is material counterevidence, but Marcus said underrepresented, not absent. limitations: The evidence is a small set of prominent documents, not a representative sample.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The scenario in which AGI is not imminent is underrepresented in current policy discussions.

statement.excerpt: And if there is any scenario that is underrepresented in current policy discussions, it’s that one.
statement.document_title: Ezra Klein’s new take on AGI – and why I think it’s probably wrong

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that prominent policy discussions give insufficient serious consideration to AGI taking substantially longer than the next two to three years.
The surrounding discussion principally concerns US and UK policy. These are the main jurisdictions assessed, without treating them as the entire worldwide discussion.

Because no reporting period is specified, the target is the current 2025 policy discussion through publication. Individual documents can establish consideration of a scenario, but cannot establish its overall representation.
Underrepresentation requires a defensible comparison of attention and substantive treatment. Equal airtime is not assumed.
criteria.support_condition: A representative set of contemporaneous policy records shows systematically little substantive consideration of non-imminent AGI, relative to imminent AGI, under a justified comparison.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative records show substantial consideration of non-imminent AGI commensurate with the acknowledged uncertainty. Isolated counterexamples alone do not settle the claim.
